documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence General Use Guidelines
documents.summary: UW-IT general-use guidelines for generative AI, mostly about data privacy, approved tools, and user responsibility. A short acceptable-use section hands the course-level rule to instructors and tells students to follow it.
documents.stance_why: The page says the University 'supports the responsible use of generative AI' and sets conditions (approved tools for university data, review of output, disclosure), so AI is permitted with conditions. The course-specific decision is left to instructors, but most of the document's text sets conditions of use rather than delegating.

units.why: The opening sentence states the university's overall position that it 'supports the responsible use of generative AI', a framework statement of purpose and principle, so P56 with a permit stance addressed to everyone.
units.anchor: The University supports the responsible use of generative AI (GenAI) when helpful to further its

units.why: 'Only UW-approved services and applications may be used with University data' limits GenAI to approved tools, which is the use-approved-tools type (P92) rather than a course tool (P17) because it is institution-wide.
units.anchor: Only UW-approved services and applications may be used with University data

units.why: This says UWIT 'can review tools and use cases' to inform unit decisions on approval, an institutional tool-review service, so P65.
units.anchor: UWIT can review tools and use cases to help inform unit decisions about whether to

units.why: 'All use of GenAI must comply with all relevant UW policies and standards' requires compliance with existing university policy, which is P77.
units.anchor: All use of GenAI must comply with all relevant UW policies and standards

units.why: The sentence offers 'complimentary training, tool review, architectural guidance, and security assessments', an institutional offer of AI training; P70 fits best since it is not faculty-only.
units.anchor: Complimentary training, tool review, architectural guidance, and security assessments are available
units.fit_note: Also offers tool review, architectural guidance and security assessments, which P70 does not capture.

units.why: 'You are ultimately responsible and accountable for your use of GenAI and all outcomes' makes users own what results from AI, P29.
units.anchor: You are ultimately responsible and accountable for your use of GenAI and all outcomes derived

units.why: 'Students must adhere to policies and rules applicable to their course or project' puts on students the duty to follow the rules that apply to them, P78 (not P10, which is about asking when unsure).
units.anchor: Students must adhere to policies and rules applicable to their course or project

units.why: 'Course instructors have the discretion to allow, prohibit, or put parameters around the use of GenAI' hands the decision to instructors, P04.

units.policy: You must review GenAI output before using or publishing it.

units.why: 'GenAI may enhance, but does not replace, human judgment, particularly in decision-making affecting individuals' keeps a human in decisions about people, so P73.
units.anchor: GenAI may enhance, but does not replace, human judgment

units.why: 'Avoid GenAI use that may reinforce inappropriate biases or create barriers for underrepresented groups' names bias and equity harms, P53 with should-not.
units.anchor: Avoid GenAI use that may reinforce inappropriate biases or create barriers for underrepresented groups

units.why: 'Disclosing GenAI use is often advisable and may be mandatory' addresses disclosure, noting failure may have serious consequences in coursework, so P24 (not P28, since it states no safe-harbor rule).

units.why: 'Maintain detailed records of GenAI use' is a recordkeeping duty; nearest type is P26 (keep logs) though here records serve compliance and personal data, not submission to an instructor.
units.anchor: Maintain detailed records of GenAI use, especially when personal data is involved
units.fit_note: Records are for privacy and compliance (a personal data inventory), not transcripts submitted to an instructor.

units.why: 'Ensure compliance with records protection and preservation laws' ties AI use to existing law, P77.
units.anchor: Ensure compliance with records protection and preservation laws

units.why: Public (Level 1) data 'can be used with GenAI' sets which data are safe to enter, which belongs with protecting data, P50.

units.anchor: Do not use data that is restricted

units.fit_note: Review is triggered by a high-risk use case of decisions about people, not by a tool or contract.

units.why: 'Report suspected security and privacy incidents immediately' gives a reporting channel for AI-related incidents, P71.
units.anchor: Report suspected security and privacy incidents immediately
units.fit_note: The sentence concerns general security and privacy incidents, not only AI ones.

units.why: The page lists the 'UW AI Community of Practice', Task Force and town halls, community engagement on AI, so P88.

units.policy: UW has an AI Community of Practice, an AI Task Force, Town Halls, and an AI Perspectives Speaker Series.

documents.unit: Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
documents.title: Guidelines for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Research (Schoolwide Policies page)
documents.summary: The Allen School's unit-wide guidelines for AI in research, covering accuracy, data privacy, peer review confidentiality and disclosure to co-authors and advisors. They do not cover coursework.
documents.stance_why: The section says 'If and when AI is used in research, it must be used responsibly', which allows AI with conditions (verification, privacy, disclosure), so permit.

units.anchor: norms governing the use of AI in research

units.why: 'Human authors remain fully responsible for the integrity of their work' puts responsibility on authors, P29.
units.anchor: Human authors remain fully responsible for the integrity of their work

units.why: 'Generative AI tools can produce incorrect statements, fabricated citations' is a warning that output is often wrong, P31.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools can produce incorrect statements, fabricated citations

units.why: 'you are accountable for any errors they introduce, just as if you had written the material yourself' is ownership of output, P29.

units.fit_note: Disclosure is to co-authors, and it also requires verifying content.

units.anchor: You are responsible for understanding and following the policies of the venue you are reviewing
